explanations.why: Part3.pdf explicitly names the SG UNIT-2 FLR WASH WTR TRANSFER PUMPS as 2W, which is corroborated by Part4.pdf p.58, and matches the proposed change implying they are not yet 1 working. Part1.pdf p.43 refers to SG UNIT-2 WASTE WATER TRANSFER PUMPS, which appears to be different equipment or a misattributed quote.
explanations.consequence: If 1 working pump is assumed to already exist, engineers might skip upgrading pump capacity or adding standby controls, leaving the plant with half the required 105M3/HR per-pump flow capacity when running only one pump.

explanations.why: Part3.pdf directly names the SG UNIT-2 floor wash water transfer pumps with a 2W arrangement (matching Part4.pdf p.58), whereas Part1.pdf p.43 describes SG UNIT-2 waste water transfer pumps as 1W+1S.
explanations.consequence: If the 1W+1S arrangement from Part1.pdf is treated as the existing baseline instead of 2W, necessary piping, valve, and auto-start modifications for converting to standby operation may be omitted, causing flooding if the single running pump fails or cannot handle full floor wash flow.
